Two answers make the difference in almost every report of this kind, and neither
of them is obvious from the outside. They are the first two questions below.
Please answer them even if you are not sure they are relevant.

### What the task asked

The question a volunteer was shown and the answers they could give. Paste the
campaign definition if you still have it.

### What the consensus rule was

How many answers a subject needed, and how those answers were turned into one
label. If you did not change it, say that you used the default and give the
version, because the default has changed between releases before.

### Which subjects look wrong

Identifiers, or an excerpt of the export, for a handful of subjects where you
disagree with the label. A few concrete ones are more useful than a description
of the pattern.

### What you expected those subjects to come out as

For each one, the label you think it should have had.

### What the volunteers actually answered

If you can see the individual answers behind those subjects, include them. This
is what separates a consensus rule that is behaving as designed from a defect in
how answers were recorded.

### Version and deployment shape

The release tag, whether the model was switched on, and anything you changed from
the defaults.
